rule: A player gets its own page only if it holds a seat, licence or charter that changes where money settles, or operates a rail; a practitioner in that market knows the name without searching; and the row cites a primary source. Same-function players share one grouped page. One company, one page.

groups.name: The Clearing House (CHIPS and RTP)
groups.line: Bank-owned operator of two US systems. CHIPS nets large dollar payments between banks. RTP is an instant system funded from a joint account at the Federal Reserve.

groups.name: US clearing and correspondent banks
groups.line: Large banks that clear dollars for other banks, at home and across borders. Most cross-border dollar payments pass through one of them.

groups.name: US sponsor banks
groups.line: Small and mid-size US banks that hold the charter and the deposits behind fintech apps and card programs. The fintech runs the product. The bank holds the money and the regulatory duty.

groups.name: Banking as a service middleware
groups.line: Software between fintech programs and sponsor banks. Holds no customer money itself.

groups.name: Card issuer processors
groups.line: Run card issuing and ledgers for whoever holds the licence. The issuing bank holds the money.

groups.name: Novel US charters
groups.line: Newer charters, such as Wyoming special purpose depository institutions and national trust banks, testing how close a nonbank model can get to the Federal Reserve.

groups.name: Stablecoin issuers
groups.line: Issue dollar and euro tokens backed by reserves held at banks and in short-term government debt. The token moves on a public ledger. The reserves stay in the banking system.

groups.name: Payment companies with their own TARGET access
groups.line: Licensed payment and e-money companies in the euro area that hold their own account in TARGET, now that the ECB allows it.

groups.name: Payment companies in Pix directly
groups.line: Brazilian payment institutions that connect to Pix and settle on their own account at the central bank, without a bank in between.

groups.name: Card push rails (Visa Direct, Mastercard Move)
groups.line: The card networks' services for pushing money to a card or account, at home and across borders.

groups.name: Cross-border payout networks
groups.line: Reach bank accounts, wallets and cash in many countries through local partner banks. The sender's provider prefunds them.

groups.name: FX and hard-to-reach currencies
groups.line: Convert currencies and supply liquidity on the far side so payouts land already funded.

groups.name: Remittance apps
groups.line: Collect money in one country and pay it out in another, to a bank, a wallet or cash.

groups.name: Emerging market collection agents
groups.line: Collect local payments such as Pix or cash vouchers for global merchants that have no local entity, then pay out abroad.
